Job Description

LYNX is seeking an experienced Diesel & CNG Electronic Systems Technician also known at LYNX as a Technician A - Electronics to inspect, diagnose, maintain, and repair electronic and electrical systems used in transit operations. Equipment includes fair boxes, destination signs, communication systems, video recording equipment, and other onboard electronic devices.  This position performs preventative and corrective maintenance, troubleshoots complex system failures, interprets wiring diagrams and schematics, and tests equipment to verify reliable operation.  The technician also documents repairs and provides technician guidance to other technicians while following established safety procedures. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Shifts: Must be willing and able to work any and all shifts below as LYNX is a 24/7 operation and this will include weekends and holidays:

  • 6:00am to 2:30pm 
  • 4:00am to 2:30pm 
  • 6:00pm to 4:30am (This shift comes with a $2.00 pay differential)

Essential Functions

  • Completes scheduled and non-scheduled maintenance on all electronic systems, subassemblies and control devices.
  • Inspects, diagnoses, removes, and repairs electronic systems, equipment and devices.
  • Records periodic electrical testing and recommends modification or replacement of equipment that fails to meet acceptable operational standards.
  • Diagnoses the cause of electrical or mechanical malfunction or failure of operational equipment and performs preventive or corrective maintenance.
  • Applies electrical theory and related knowledge to test and repair operational electrical and electrical controlled equipment and circuitry.
  • Adjusts, calibrates, aligns and modifies circuitry and components, and records effects on unit performance.
  • Analyzes and interprets test data.
  • Develops charts, graphs and schematics to describe and illustrate system’s operating characteristics, malfunctions, deviations from design specifications and functional limitations for consideration by management in broader determinations affecting system design.
  • Uses testing equipment (meters, oscilloscopes, test bench and mock-up).
  • Executes field repairs on all electronic systems, subassemblies and control devices including connector and harness manufacture and repair.
  • Works with lower-grade technicians on difficult or unusual problems.
  • Ensures operator defects are completed on all electrical equipment on schedule.
  • Sets up standard test apparatus or devices, test equipment and circuitry to conduct functional, operational, environmental, and live test to evaluate performance and reliability of production models.
  • Performs other duties as may be required or assigned.

  • Electronic Technician Degree helpful.
  • Must possess and maintain a current Florida CDL permit/license, Class “B” with Passenger endorsement and Airbrakes.

  • Knowledge of electronics to inspect, diagnose, remove and repair equipment and systems.
  • Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions of the trade.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to read electrical wiring diagrams and schematics
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work as a team player.
  • Ability to drive buses, trucks, non-revenue vehicles and equipment into the shop, line and yard.
  • Ability to physically bend, stoop, walk, kneel, stretch and lift fifty pounds.
  • Ability to work days, nights, weekends, and holidays.
  • Ability to pass DOT physical and drug screen.
  • Ability to understand and operate special test equipment.
  • Ability to work in open bays, inside buses and inside test and repair room.
  • Ability to work with commercial cleaners and toxic materials.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English, both orally and in writing.

Full job description

Join Our Team and Drive Excellence in Fleet Maintenance!

Are you a skilled diesel or heavy vehicle maintenance professional with a passion for teaching and developing others? LYNX is seeking a Maintenance Training Instructor (Diesel & CNG) to lead, develop, and deliver engaging technical training programs that empower our maintenance team to keep Central Forida moving safely and efficiently. 

In this impactful role, you'll combine your hands-on maintenance expertise with your ability to train, mentor, and inspire technicians at all levels.  From developing training materials and conducting hands-on instructions to evaluating program effectiveness and supporting regulatory compliance, you'll play a key role in building a highly skilled workforce that supports one of the region's largest public transportation systems. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Hours of Operation:

Monday-Friday 6am-2:30pm but can work any 8-hour shifts that are needed and we are open 7 days a week depending on training needs, some shifts might be overnight. We are a 24/7 operation; however, we will provide advanced notice 

Day in the Life:

This position develops, coordinates, implements, conducts and evaluates training programs for maintenance personnel in the proper service, repair and maintenance of buses, support vehicles, and shop equipment.
This position is considered safety‐sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.
Essential Functions: This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job. All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

In conjunction with the above, the Diesel Maintenance Instructor will:


• Consults with Maintenance department leadership for input in developing maintenance training programs.
• Delivers effective training programs by applying strong presentation, training and facilitation skills, and delivering feedback to learners; develops action plans and measures the impact to the organization.
• Prepares, plans, organizes and conducts maintenance training needs assessments and analyses, lesson plans, course curricula, visual and mechanical aides, written materials and hands‐on instruction that complies with internal procedures and external mandates or regulations.
• Participates as a resource to maintenance management on safety, technical proficiency and productivity issues, and works with the safety division to develop and implement programs compliant with state and national regulations, to promote the safety and well‐being of Authority employees.
• Coordinates, evaluates and monitors internal and external vendor training programs.
• Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of training programs by measuring changes in skill levels and improvements demonstrated by maintenance personnel and modifies programs accordingly to improve effectiveness to the quality vehicle maintenance training programs.
• Ensures that all training materials are updated as needed, for new equipment, new procedures, technical information, etc.

• Additional directly related experience beyond the minimum requirement may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.
